 APM Steps Up Monitoring To Track Flood Reports In Five States
 18/11/2026 06:49 PM 
 IPOH, Nov 18 (Bernama) -- The Malaysian Civil Defence Force (APM) is stepping up surveillance, including on social media, to identify reports of flooding in five states amid the current situation.
 Its deputy chief commissioner (Operations), Ghazali Abd Rahman, said APM continuously reviews reports posted on social media so relevant authorities can act early.
 "All information, including that shared on social media, is currently being monitored by personnel at APM's District Operations Control Centres nationwide, particularly in flood-hit areas.
-->
 "Upon receiving information, APM will continue to mobilise its teams and respond immediately to rescue flood victims, without any time restrictions," he said.
 He said this at a press conference after attending the Perak APM personnel appreciation ceremony at the Perak State Civil Defence Office here today.
 APM will deploy 7,000 full-time officers and personnel to deal with flooding in several states caused by the Northeast Monsoon, which occurs annually between November and March.
 On the flood situation in affected locations, Ghazali said the situation was under control, with disaster management teams at state and district levels monitoring developments closely.
 "This includes assets, logistics and personnel in the respective states, which are considered sufficient to manage every disaster incident without the need to mobilise assistance across state borders for the time being,” he said.
